text.p: Highlights of the five world
championships:
Helsinki 1983
Carl Lewis at the peak of his powers wins the 100 metres and
long jump before anchoring the U.S. team to a world record in
the 4x100 metres relay. Mary Decker defeats the best of the
eastern Europeans in the 1,500 and 3,000 metres but the position
is reversed in the sprints where East Germans Marlies Goehr and
Marita Koch win the 100 and 200 respectively.
Jarmila Kratochvilova, at the age of 32, sets a world record
in the women's 400 metres and also wins the 800 metres. Steve
Cram wins the 1,500 and favourites Rob de Castella and Grete
Waitz both take gold in the men's and women's marathons.
In the field events, Sergei Bubka captures the first of five
world pole vault titles and Heike Drechsler wins the women's
long jump.
Rome 1987
Ben Johnson defeats Lewis in the men's 100 metres final in
9.83 seconds, a tenth of a second faster than the previous world
record. The mark is expunged from the books and Lewis awarded
the title after Johnson tests positive for steroids following
his win in the 1988 Seoul Olympic final.
Stefka Kostadinova sets a world record in the women's high
jump and the Kenyan men make a significant impact with Billy
Konchellah winning the 800 metres, Paul Kipkoech the 10,000 and
Douglas Wakiihuri the marathon.
Silke Gladisch wins the women's 100 and 200 metres double and
Ed Moses retains the men's 400 metres hurdles title, his last
major title.
Tokyo 1991
Mike Powell breaks Bob Beamon's 23-year-old world long jump
record with a leap of 8.95 metres while Lewis, in his greatest
track performance, wins the men's 100 metres final in a world
record 9.86 seconds.
Noureddine Morceli, Moses Kiptanui and Dan O'Brien each win
the first of three consecutive world titles in the 1,500 metres,
3,000 metres steeplechase and decathlon.
Michael Johnson takes his first global title with a
comprehensive win in the 200 metres and Katrin Krabbe completes
a golden 100-200 metres double.
Stuttgart 1993
Linford Christie follows up his Barcelona Olympic gold with
an equally sweeping victory in the 100 metres.
His British team mates Colin Jackson and Sally Gunnell set
world records in the 110 metres hurdles and 400 metres hurdles
respectively.
Merlene Ottey, denied victory in the 100 metres on a
photo-finish, wins her first global title with a narrow victory
in the 200. Chinese women dominate the track with wins to Liu
Dong in the 1,500, Qu Yunxia in the 3,000 and Wang Junxia in the
Gothenburg 1995
Michael Johnson clinches the first global 200-400 metres
double and Jonathan Edwards leaps a world record 18.29 metres in
the triple jump.
Kim Batten breaks Gunnell's world record in the 400 metres
hurdles with second-placed Tonja Buford also going under the old
mark.
Moses Kiptanui, with the world 3,000 metres steeplechase
record seemingly at his mercy, slows up and admits later he was
saving himself for the Zurich meeting and a lucrative bonus.
